title: The Last Gravity Again
premise: Sebastian Nystrom, an insurance investigator who catalogues the colony world Vesper's impossible accidents, is the only person who still tends a gravity beacon no record shows anyone commissioning. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream of a burning fleet, Sebastian discovers the beacon is transmitting their dream outward — and that the 'accidents' he investigates are the war's edge bleeding through. The message the children carry is a peace offering from the enemy's own dead, and delivering it means betraying the colonial authority that raised him. In the end, Sebastian broadcasts the message as the jump window closes, ending the war but erasing his own records from every archive — leaving him, at last, belonging to no one and to everyone.
about_author: Theo Zhou is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction about losses among the stars. They write from a coastal town where the fog arrives on schedule, like gravity.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Sebastian performs his monthly maintenance on the unnamed gravity beacon, logging its impossible power draw for an insurer that no longer exists. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as routine — he loves this machine more than any person.

chapters.title: Actuarial Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Investigating a farmer whose tractor fell upward, Sebastian finds the same anomaly signature in eleven other files spanning thirty years. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: The Children's Dream
chapters.summary: At the schoolhouse, forty children independently describe the same dream: a fleet of ships burning in formation above a green world. POV: Mara, a nine-year-old who draws it perfectly. Emotional beat: wonder shading into fear.

chapters.title: A Claim Against the Sky
chapters.summary: Sebastian files the falling-tractor report; Colonial Authority auditor Ilsa Reyes flags him for surveillance, noting his beacon access logs. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: suspicion with a flicker of reluctant respect.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Deep in the beacon's firmware, Sebastian finds a message queue addressed to coordinates inside enemy space — queued before the colony was founded. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: vertigo; his one constant thing has been lying to him.

chapters.title: The Dream Spreads
chapters.summary: Adults begin dreaming the burning fleet too; a dockworker sleepwalks into the sea and survives, insisting he was 'catching someone.' POV: Mara's mother, Adaeze. Emotional beat: communal dread, tenderness toward frightened children.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Tea
chapters.summary: Ilsa summons Sebastian for a friendly interrogation that is anything but; he lies badly about the beacon and she lets him leave anyway. POV: alternating Sebastian/Ilsa. Emotional beat: two lonely people recognizing each other across a table of lies.

chapters.title: The First Accident That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Sebastian reopens his oldest case file and realizes the 'impossible accidents' form a pattern spelling out orbital mechanics — a trajectory. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: revelation as grief; his career was a message he never read.

chapters.title: Jump Window Mathematics
chapters.summary: Astrogator Wen Li calculates that the next alignment opens in nineteen days — the only window a message could physically reach the enemy fleet. POV: Wen Li. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the universe offers exactly one chance.

chapters.title: They Sent Us Their Dead
chapters.summary: Decoding the beacon's origin, Sebastian learns the children's dream is a recording: the enemy fleet's dying broadcast, asking to come home. POV: Mara, dreaming fully now. Emotional beat: compassion breaking through fear of the other.

chapters.title: The Authority Decides
chapters.summary: Colonial command votes to jam the beacon and treat the dreams as psychological warfare; Ilsa is ordered to arrest Sebastian. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a noose she tied herself.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Sebastian goes underground with Wen Li and Adaeze's family, planning to hold the beacon open against the jamming. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: fugitive calm — for once, every choice is his own.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Colony
chapters.summary: Ilsa tracks them but hesitates; Sebastian shows her the decoded message and her certainty cracks. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal — she must choose which loyalty is hers.

chapters.title: Sabotage at Relay Seven
chapters.summary: Authority engineers destroy a relay node; Wen Li takes a near-fatal dose repairing it manually. POV: Wen Li. Emotional beat: sacrifice without drama — just hands doing what hands must.

chapters.title: The Children March
chapters.summary: The colony's children walk out of school toward the beacon, drawn by the dream; parents follow, then garrison soldiers refuse orders to stop them. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: innocence as irresistible force.

chapters.title: Window Opens
chapters.summary: With six hours left, Sebastian reaches the beacon under fire; Ilsa arrives not to arrest him but to stand between him and the strike team. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Sebastian uplinks the full broadcast — the enemy dead's plea and the colony children's answering song recorded at the march. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the climax as an act of translation, not violence.

chapters.title: Answering Fire
chapters.summary: The enemy fleet holds fire; a single shuttle crosses the gap carrying survivors of the original generation ship both worlds descended from. POV: Ilsa watching from the ground. Emotional beat: awe, and the collapse of every category of 'enemy.'

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Miracle
chapters.summary: Armistice talks begin; the Authority, needing scapegoats, moves to erase Sebastian's records and charge him retroactively. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: bitter taste of victory; institutions metabolize even grace.

chapters.title: The Erasure
chapters.summary: Sebastian discovers the beacon, fulfilling its purpose, has purged every trace of him from colonial archives — he is officially never born. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: liberation disguised as loss.

chapters.title: Belonging to Everyone
chapters.summary: Mara and the other children, who all remember him, find Sebastian living quietly at the beacon; the colony's new joint council grants him sanctuary. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: chosen family replacing official identity.

chapters.title: The Last Gravity
chapters.summary: One year later, Sebastian tends the beacon still — now a lighthouse for two peoples — and finally sleeps, dreaming nothing at all, or perhaps everything. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity rewritten as relationship rather than record.
